posts.text: Why the ₹34,700 cr TAM is wrong: Wrong choice one — using total waste generation as tradeable supply. Taking India’s annual e-waste generation (7.8 MMT, though CPCB’s official number is 1.4 MMT and NITI Aayog’s higher estimate is 6.19 MMT including informal-sector waste) as if all of it flowed through the exchange. But certificates are only generated when waste is formally recycled by an authorized processor . posts.author: Aiyappaa
posts.community: MSTC Ltd.: Growth through to E-Commerce
posts.text: A rule called Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) makes the company that manufactures a product responsible for ensuring that its waste is collected and recycled after use. Companies that recycle waste receive recycling certificates, with each certificate representing a specific quantity of waste that has been properly recycled. Companies that are unable to meet their recycling obligation can instead comply by purchasing these certificates.
